en.title: Requests Dropped When Threads Run Out
en.description:
A positive event adds that many threads, and −1 represents a request. A request consumes and destroys one thread, and it is dropped if no thread is available; find the total number dropped. This is not sliding-window rate limiting.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site, and missing numeric bounds are explicitly marked as site additions.
en.input: The first line contains n, followed by the event array; 1≤n≤100000, and each element is −1 or 1..10000.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 1; 2; 0. These answers have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Track the number of available threads in order; when a request arrives, decrement it if a thread is available, otherwise count a drop.
